papers_read.title_as_printed: Alzheimer's Disease Prediction Algorithm Based on Group Convolution and a Joint Loss Function (Cheng, Wang, Wei, Liu, Chen; Computational and Mathematical Methods in Medicine 2022, 1854718)
Leveraging hemispheric asymmetry in structural MRI with an attention-guided 3D CNN for early prediction of Alzheimer's conversion (Liu, Yao, Liu, Li, Zeng, Xu; Neural Networks 197 (2026) 108534)

what_each_reports.P-218: Three-class cross-sectional diagnosis (AD vs MCI vs NC) from 18F-FDG PET: 2D slices of SPM-normalised PET, grouped-convolution ResNet18 with hybrid attention and a centre-loss term. Training ADNI-1 (190 AD / 350 MCI / 200 NC per text), test ADNI-2 (124 AD / 192 MCI / 84 NC); Table 3 also lists K_fold 10. Best: ACC 89.4%, AUC 92.3% (SEN 87.43 / SPE 88.26, with AD and MCI both counted as positives). No conversion endpoint.
what_each_reports.P-65: MCI-to-AD conversion within 36 months (300 pMCI / 273 sMCI, right-handed ADNI-1/2/3/GO) from single baseline T1 sMRI with HemiNet (DenseNet-121 3D CNN plus hemispheric asymmetry modules), five-fold stratified CV repeated five times: AUC 0.8401 +/- 0.0297, ACC 0.7819. External OASIS-3 (62 sMCI / 82 pMCI): AUC 0.8137, ACC 0.7345.

quantity_a: AUC of 3-class AD/MCI/NC diagnostic classification (current diagnosis, no horizon) from FDG-PET slices, ADNI-1 train / ADNI-2 test.
quantity_b: AUC of predicting 36-month conversion to AD among people with MCI (pMCI vs sMCI) from baseline structural MRI, ADNI 5-fold CV (external OASIS-3 0.81).
incompatible_if_same: No. Even for a shared task, two different architectures each reporting their own AUC, with neither evaluating the other's model, would not be incompatible.

gates.task: mismatch: P-218 is 3-way diagnosis AD/MCI/NC (registry T3), P-65 is MCI conversion prognosis (T2); the record's 'T2' for P-218 is wrong
gates.validation_tier: match: both internal ADNI evaluation (P-218 ADNI-1 to ADNI-2 split; P-65 5-fold CV), with P-65 adding an external OASIS-3 test
gates.modality_family: mismatch: P-218 is FDG-PET only; P-65 is structural MRI only (the record's 'structural_mri' for both is wrong)

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: both report ROC AUC, but on different endpoints (3-class current diagnosis vs binary 36-month conversion) and from different imaging modalities; P-218 does not say how its 3-class AUC is averaged.
performance_validity: flag does not apply: 0.923 and 0.840 are below 0.97.
independence: Distinct author groups (Anhui University vs Chongqing Normal University/Chongqing Medical University); both draw on ADNI.
grounds: P-218 classifies current diagnosis into AD, MCI or NC, whereas P-65 predicts which MCI patients convert to AD within 36 months, so the two AUCs are on different endpoints.
P-218 uses FDG-PET and P-65 uses structural MRI, so the modality-family gate fails and no waiver is on record.
The record labels both as T2 and structural MRI; both labels are wrong for P-218.

We use 190 AD cases, 350 MCI cases, and 200 NC cases among PET images as the training data from ADNI-1. Four hundred PET images are selected as the test data from ADNI-2.

record_defects: claim_a 'P-218: AUC 92.3 on T2' mislabels the task: 92.3% is a 3-class AD/MCI/NC diagnostic AUC; P-218 has no conversion endpoint (its registry row says T3).
modality_family 'structural_mri' and modality_family_equal 'Yes' are wrong: P-218 is FDG-PET only.
task_equal 'Yes' is wrong (diagnosis vs conversion prognosis).
P-218's own sample counts are inconsistent (text: 190/350/200 training; Table 1: AD 190, MCI 250, NC 200).
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing in either PDF: P-218 would need an MCI-conversion experiment on structural MRI for the two to share a quantity.
